messages.content: Okay, let me dive into this. I'll start by understanding what kind of visual you want.
Clear — I need to build a visual visual from scratch. Checking available engines...
Alright, 7 tasks queued. I'm moving through the pipeline now.

I'm coding a magnetic dipole field function using the proper vector equations (B-field proportional to 1/r³), instanced mesh particles for the iron filings that rotate to match local field tangents, TubeGeometry with emissive shaders for the curved flux lines, raycasting for draggable magnet interaction, and a domain visualization with thousands of tiny arrows representing electron spins that flip orientation when the external field is applied.

Spinning up the Three.js sandbox with OrbitControls for free camera navigation, setting up soft ambient lighting plus directional lights to make the glowing field lines pop, and initializing the animation loop that dynamically recalculates particle orientations whenever the user drags the interactive magnet.

I've built an interactive 3D physics lab where you can actually see the invisible magnetic field rendered as glowing flux lines and responsive iron particles, drag magnets together to watch attraction or repulsion happen in real-time, and switch to atomic view to understand that magnetism is really just the organized alignment of electron spins.
